name: SOFIA
aliases: Study of Fesoterodine in an Aging Population
question: Does flexible-dose fesoterodine improve urgency compared with placebo in older adults with overactive bladder?

arms.label: Fesoterodine 4 mg daily with optional increase to 8 mg
matching placebo with sham dose adjustment

design.population: Adults aged 65 years or older with at least 3 months of overactive bladder symptoms, at least eight daily micturitions and three daily urgency episodes, moderate bladder bother, and MMSE score at least 20; 47% were male and 46% had urgency urinary incontinence at baseline, and mean baseline MMSE was about 28 in both arms.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 186–187; Results, p 187; Table 1

verdictNote: Primary urgency endpoint met; urgency urinary incontinence did not differ significantly.
takeaway: In adults aged 65 or older with overactive bladder, flexible-dose fesoterodine reduced daily urgency episodes more than placebo at 12 weeks (adjusted mean changes −3.47 vs −1.92; P<0.001); among the 46% with baseline urgency incontinence, median episode change did not differ (P=0.73).

reports.label: 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: Wagg A, Khullar V, Marschall-Kehrel D, et al. "Flexible-Dose Fesoterodine in Elderly Adults with Overactive Bladder: Results of the Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of Fesoterodine in an Aging Population Trial." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2013;61(2):185-193. doi:10.1111/jgs.12088

results.measure: Change from baseline in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.note: Least-squares mean change with last observation carried forward; adjusted between-arm difference and its 95% CI were not reported.
The endpoint was analyzed only in the 46% with baseline UUI; exact subgroup denominators and a between-arm CI were not reported.
Mean MMSE change; no formal cognitive endpoint hypothesis was reported.

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per 24 hours at week 12
results.note: Least-squares mean changes; no between-arm confidence interval reported.

results.measure: No UUI episodes before weeks 8 and 12 among participants with baseline UUI
results.note: Baseline-UUI subgroup; exact arm denominators not reported.

harms.label: Urinary retention and catheterization
harms.note: Three men and two women receiving fesoterodine had retention; all catheterized patients were men.

harms.label: Any adverse event and adverse-event discontinuation
harms.note: Safety population; discontinuation values are all-causality adverse events.

delivery.label: Dose adjustment
delivery.value: Fesoterodine began at 4 mg; increase to 8 mg was allowed at week 4 or 8, with de-escalation to 4 mg at week 8; placebo adjustments were sham.

delivery.label: Dose escalation choice by week 8
delivery.locator: Full text, Participants and Dosing, p 187
delivery.note: Fesoterodine versus sham placebo adjustment; counts and denominators were not reported.

delivery.value: Of 655 randomized-phase completers, 654 entered (313 prior fesoterodine; 341 prior placebo) and 581 completed (282 and 299, respectively). Prior-placebo patients began fesoterodine 4 mg with optional increase to 8 mg at extension week 4 or 8; prior-fesoterodine patients continued their assigned dose.
